claim: A canonical evidence record must keep research topic, bounded capability, and scientific conclusion categories distinct while recording alternatives, disanalogies and falsifiers.

evidence_channels.access_evidence: Reconstructed canonical invariant; no external literature claim.
Repository test/CI status is explicitly bounded as validation metadata, not scientific evidence.
Canonical record requires an explicit access grade and access evidence field.

alternative_explanations: Record may be a category/schema design guard rather than an empirical claim.
Observed repository validation may reflect implementation correctness only.
A source provenance label may reflect publication origin without direct full-text verification.

disanalogies.difference: Generic infrastructure guard is not the CSOMI research packet or literature dossier.
Repository validation differs from scientific or phenomenological evidence.
Primary publication provenance differs from directly verified access level.

falsifiers.condition: A record or workflow treats passing tests or CI as evidence that a system has subjectivity.
A canonical record assigns one object simultaneously as research topic, capability and scientific conclusion.
A conclusion-bearing record omits alternative explanations or disanalogies.
